_comment: Hand-reviewed corrections to classify_rows.py's heuristic proposals. Every entry here was a case where the heuristic's label-pattern match either missed a row or (more importantly) would have left it defaulting to the overridable kinds (ref/method) when clinical judgement says it should be locked (dx/target/cutoff/note). Each entry carries the reasoning in _why so a later reviewer can check it, not just trust it. Applied by classify_rows.py on top of the heuristics; see app/classify_rows.py and SCHEMA.md.

r4._why: INR target for a mechanical mitral valve (typically 2.5-3.5) is a treatment target, not the population's normal INR.

r1._why: SAAG 1.1 is a single diagnostic split point (portal vs non-portal cause of ascites), not a population reference interval.

r2._why: Same cutoff, the other side of the same split.
Hyperketonaemia describes the abnormal/action state, not a population's normal range.

r3._why: Intermediate enzyme activity is a carrier-state diagnostic category, not a reference interval.

r4._why: Beta-thalassaemia trait is a diagnostic finding, not the normal HbA2 reference range.

r2._why: Severity bands of a diagnosed disease (haemophilia A), not reference ranges for an undiagnosed population.

r3._why: Same — moderate haemophilia A severity band.

r4._why: Same — severe haemophilia A severity band.

r3._why: Diagnostic classification (possible type 1 VWD), not a reference interval.

r4._why: Adequacy criterion for a dynamic stimulation test (Synacthen) is a diagnostic judgement, not a baseline diurnal reference value.

r3._why: "Preserved beta-cell function" is an interpretive diagnostic category, not a reference range.
Ovarian-reserve classification band, not a reference interval for a demographic population.

r2._why: Severity band (moderate elevation), not a reference range.

r3._why: Severity band (intermediate), not a reference range.

r2._why: The CK-MB/total-CK relative index is a diagnostic index with its own interpretive cutoff for cardiac origin, not a reference range.

r3._why: TDM test: there is no 'normal' lithium level in an unmedicated person. The elderly-preferred value is a dosing target, same as the adult rows.

r4._why: Toxicity threshold, not a treatment target.

r2._why: TDM test — the AF 'usual range' is a dosing target, same reasoning as the heart-failure row (already auto-classified target).

r3._why: Describes an abnormal clinical state (obvious intoxication) tied to a level, not a population reference range.

r1._why: TDM test — transplant immunosuppressant trough target, not a population reference range (there is no normal tacrolimus level in an untreated person).

r3._why: Same — ciclosporin early post-transplant target.

r1._why: A timepoint decision threshold for leucovorin rescue after high-dose methotrexate, not a reference range or an aspirational target.

r3._why: Same — 72h rescue decision point.
Aldosterone:renin ratio screen-positive threshold for primary aldosteronism is a diagnostic cutoff, not a reference range.

r1._why: Post-treatment response category (excellent response), a diagnostic classification specific to a treated cancer patient, not a reference interval.

r3._why: Same — biochemical incomplete response category.

r4._why: Caveat explaining the marker is not interpretable in this setting, not a numeric range of any kind.

r3._why: Myeloma ISS staging criterion, not a reference range.

r6._why: The IMWG myeloma-defining event criterion is a diagnostic threshold, not a reference range.

r4._why: A level 'supportive of Wilson disease' is a diagnostic threshold, not the population reference range (already given separately as r3).

r3._why: Marginal status is a deficiency classification band, not a reference range.
A level 'markedly raised' consistent with rhabdomyolysis is a diagnostic threshold, not a reference range.
Increased fragility is an abnormal diagnostic finding (e.g. hereditary spherocytosis), not a reference range.

r4._why: Decreased fragility is likewise an abnormal diagnostic finding (e.g. thalassaemia trait).

r2._why: Light's-criteria-style exudate threshold is a diagnostic classification of the fluid, not a reference range.

r3._why: Same — LDH ratio exudate threshold.

r4._why: ADA level supporting tuberculous pericarditis is a diagnostic threshold.

r5._why: Lymphocyte predominance pointing to TB/malignancy is a diagnostic interpretation, not a reference range.

r2._why: The ≥2-bands criterion for a positive result (supporting MS) is a diagnostic threshold, not a reference range.

r4._why: Raised IgG index indicating intrathecal synthesis is a diagnostic finding, not a reference range.

r2._why: CFTR-genetics-referral band is a diagnostic classification from the CF sweat-test algorithm, not a reference range.

r3._why: Positive result consistent with CF is a diagnostic classification.

r2._why: 'Significant proteinuria' is a diagnostic severity band on 24-h protein, not the population reference range (r1 is).

r3._why: 'Nephrotic range' is a diagnostic severity band on 24-h protein, not a reference range.

r7._why: 'Nephrotic range' on PCR is the same diagnostic severity band restated for the ratio, not a reference range.

r2._why: The expected response after a water-deprivation challenge is a provocative-test pass/fail threshold (DI workup), not a baseline population reference range.

r3._why: 'Pre-renal / hypovolaemia' is a diagnostic classification of urine sodium in the AKI work-up, not a reference range.

r4._why: 'SIADH or intrinsic renal' is the other side of the same AKI-aetiology classification by urine sodium.

r5._why: 'Pre-renal' FENa is a diagnostic classification threshold (<1%), not a reference range.

r6._why: 'Intrinsic (ATN)' FENa is the other side of the same AKI-aetiology FENa classification.
